newsitem.title: USA: US debt managers limit duration exposure Apr 8 wk.
newsitem.headline: US debt managers limit duration exposure Apr 8 wk.

text.p: Money managers maintained a profile of limited duration exposure in their U.S. debt portfolios last week, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates.
"At this point, there does not appear to be an urgency to make structural changes of significance," the report said.
"Overall market sentiment remains bearish, but has improved somewhat on an asset-weighted basis," it said.
In the week ended April 8, duration bogey rose to 4.25 from 4.24 on an arithmetic basis and increased to 4.71 from 4.70 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
The survey's bear/bull index fell to 4.66 from 4.72 on an arithmetic basis. It slipped to 5.00 from 5.01 on an asset-weighted basis.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio in the past week advanced to 7.08 percent from 7.02 percent.
Twelve percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, down from 16 percent the week before.
The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active slipped to 4.33 from 5.75.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
